endorsements.quote: He described the need for rigorous multi-site testing and prospective studies before clinical use, to be sure there is evidence of its accuracy and equity ( 3 ).
He urged that AI should be as trustworthy and compassionate as the clinicians using it, augmenting physicians' clinical judgment rather than replacing it ( 4 ).

unlisted_practices: Design algorithms with transparency from the start.
Involve clinicians in AI design and training.
Foster interdisciplinary collaboration among technology developers, clinicians, policymakers, and patient stakeholders.
Use strong encryption, regulatory frameworks, and monitoring to safeguard data privacy in federated AI networks.
Keep patient data encrypted on local servers while allowing algorithms to run across sites.
Integrate clinician-derived decision rules with machine learning outputs in hybrid models to augment rather than replace physician judgment.
Deploy AI only where it offers tangible benefits rather than because it is an emerging technology.
Maintain ongoing human evaluation of clinical language models to ensure they are safe, fair, and effective.
Prioritize the algorithmically underserved, who are underrepresented in datasets, when developing AI.
